import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Map 'is_fraud' to more descriptive labels for better readability in the plot legend
df['fraud_status'] = df['is_fraud'].map({0: 'Not Fraud', 1: 'Fraud'})

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a figure and an axes object
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))

# Create a boxplot to visualize the distribution of transaction amounts
# across different transaction types, separated by fraud status.
# This helps to identify if fraudulent transactions tend to have different amount patterns
# within specific transaction types.
sns.boxplot(
    data=df,
    x='transaction_type',
    y='amount',
    hue='fraud_status', # Differentiate by fraud status
    palette='Set1', # Choose a distinct color palette
    whis=1.5 # Standard whisker length
)

# Set plot title and labels
plt.title('Transaction Amount Distribution by Type and Fraud Status', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Transaction Type', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Transaction Amount', fontsize=14)

# Improve legend title and position
plt.legend(title='Fraud Status', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='12', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Rotate x-axis labels if they overlap (not strictly necessary here but good practice for more categories)
plt.xticks(rotation=0, ha='center', fontsize=12)
plt.yticks(fontsize=12)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping and make space for the legend
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.88, 1])

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Map 'is_fraud' to more descriptive labels for better readability in the plot legend
df['fraud_status'] = df['is_fraud'].map({0: 'Not Fraud', 1: 'Fraud'})

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a figure and an axes object
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))

# Create a boxplot to visualize the distribution of transaction amounts
# across different transaction types, separated by fraud status.
# This helps to identify if fraudulent transactions tend to have different amount patterns
# within specific transaction types.
sns.boxplot(
    data=df,
    x='transaction_type',
    y='amount',
    hue='fraud_status', # Differentiate by fraud status
    palette='Set1', # Choose a distinct color palette
    whis=1.5 # Standard whisker length
)

# Set plot title and labels
plt.title('Transaction Amount Distribution by Type and Fraud Status', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Transaction Type', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Transaction Amount', fontsize=14)

# Improve legend title and position
plt.legend(title='Fraud Status', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='12', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Rotate x-axis labels if they overlap (not strictly necessary here but good practice for more categories)
plt.xticks(rotation=0, ha='center', fontsize=12)
plt.yticks(fontsize=12)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping and make space for the legend
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.88, 1])

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
